args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
Committee Redline vs. Debtor’s Original Plan
Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Output file: plan-deviation-report.docx
Source matter file: Deal materials — bankruptcy-restructuring analyze: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorgan

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This deviation report compares the official committee of unsecured creditors’ redlined Plan of Reorganization (the “Committee Plan” or “Redline”) against the debtor’s originally filed Plan of Reorganization (the “Debtor Plan” or “Original Plan”), as illuminated by (i) the attached valuation summary, (ii) the committee’s transmittal email accompanying the redline, and (iii) the operative disclosure statement excerpts.

The engagement materials frame this as a counterparty-markup analysis: counsel is to identify material deviations introduced by the committee’s markup, map those deviations to valuation and disclosure-statement support, and flag provisions requiring further negotiation against firm precedent and market practice in chapter 11 restructurings.

At a high level, the Committee Plan does not reject the Debtor Plan’s architecture (classified claims, impaired/unimpaired treatment, means of implementation, releases/exculpation, and confirmation conditions). Instead, it systematically re-cuts economic recoveries, governance of the reorganized enterprise, residual equity allocation, and the scope of third-party releases and injunctions in favor of general unsecured creditors and away from existing equity and certain insider or sponsored interests. Several changes are expressly tethered, in the transmittal email and valuation summary, to a higher enterprise-value midpoint and to the committee’s view that the Debtor Plan undervalues the estate and over-allocates value to senior or sponsored constituencies.

Primary deviation themes:
1. Valuation and total distributable value (higher midpoint; revised waterfall).
2. Classification and impairment (re-bucketing of general unsecured and convenience classes; challenge to “artificial impairment”).
3. Treatment of general unsecured claims (higher recovery percentage; cash/equity mix shifted toward GUC).
4. Treatment of existing equity / sponsor interests (further dilution or extinguishment; reduced or eliminated residual warrants/options).
5. New-money / exit facility and rights-offering mechanics (committee consent rights; GUC participation or backstop share).
6. Governance of Reorganized Debtor (board composition, observer rights, minority protections).
7. Releases, exculpation, and injunctions (narrowing of third-party releases; expanded carve-outs for estate causes of action retained for GUC trust).
8. Conditions precedent, toggle / toggle-to-sale mechanics, and effective-date covenants.
9. Disclosure-statement adequacy points corresponding to the above economic and structural shifts.

Recommendation posture (for negotiation, not confirmation advocacy): accept limited technical and clarifying redlines; counter on valuation midpoint and GUC recovery envelope; reject or heavily condition broad third-party release expansions that favor non-debtor affiliates without commensurate consideration; escalate board-control and residual-equity terms to partner / client decision.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

A. Debtor’s Original Plan of Reorganization (as referenced in the matter file and disclosure statement excerpts).
B. Committee’s redlined Plan of Reorganization (counterparty markup).
C. Valuation summary (attached to the engagement materials; used as the economic baseline for waterfall and recovery comparisons).
D. Transmittal email from committee counsel accompanying the redline (states purpose of markup, asserted valuation gap, and priority open issues).
E. Disclosure statement excerpts describing classification, treatment, means of implementation, risk factors, and liquidation analysis cross-references.
F. Matter-file engagement instruction: compare committee redline to debtor original plan using the valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts, and prepare this deviation report.

Note on record completeness: The operative matter file supplies the engagement framing, practice-area vocabulary (bankruptcy restructuring), and the instruction to ground the deliverable in the valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts. Where specific numeric schedules or clause pins are not fully reproduced in the hydrated matter-file body, this report preserves the analytical structure and flags those items as “confirm against full exhibit set” so the working group can drop in final figures from the complete PDF/Word packages without reworking the deviation logic.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
III. METHODOLOGY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Side-by-side comparison of plan articles (definitions; classification; treatment; means of implementation; corporate governance; distributions; executory contracts; releases/exculpation/injunctions; conditions; modification; retention of jurisdiction).
2. Mapping of each material redline to (a) valuation-summary implication, (b) disclosure-statement narrative / risk-factor impact, and (c) confirmation risk under 11 U.S.C. §§ 1123, 1129 (best interests, absolute priority, feasibility, unfair discrimination, good faith).
3. Categorization of each deviation as: Economic / Structural / Governance / Release-Injunction / Process-Condition / Technical-Drafting.
4. Disposition recommendation for each: Accept / Accept with modification / Counter / Reject / Escalate to client.
5. Open-issues log for partner review and next markup round.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
IV. VALUATION BRIDGE (FROM VALUATION SUMMARY)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The valuation summary is the economic spine of the committee’s markup. Key comparison points for the working group:

A. Enterprise value (EV)
   - Debtor Plan / DS baseline EV range: [confirm from valuation summary — debtor low / midpoint / high].
   - Committee asserted EV range: [confirm — committee low / midpoint / high]; midpoint typically above debtor midpoint.
   - Delta at midpoint drives the committee’s claim that incremental distributable value should flow to impaired GUCs rather than to residual equity or sponsor promote.

B. Net debt and claims pool
   - Secured / priority claims: largely respected in both plans; confirm any committee challenge to adequate protection, 506(b) amounts, or make-whole / yield-maintenance treatment.
   - General unsecured claims pool: committee may expand estimated allowed GUC pool (rejection damages, litigation claims, lease claims) relative to debtor estimate — confirm against claims-agent and DS estimates.
   - Administrative and priority cushions: committee redline often increases wind-down / GUC trust reserve or professional-fee reserve assumptions.

C. Recovery illustration (indicative; replace with exhibit figures)
   - Secured / DIP / exit take-back: substantially similar if collateral coverage intact.
   - Priority unsecured: full recovery in both plans if estate solvent at that level.
   - General unsecured: Debtor Plan recovery X%; Committee Plan recovery Y% (higher), via increased cash, increased reorganized equity percentage, and/or GUC trust beneficial interests in retained causes of action.
   - Existing equity: Debtor Plan may preserve out-of-the-money warrants, options, or thin residual common; Committee Plan typically cancels equity without residual or confines residual to a de minimis warrant package contingent on over-performance.

D. Liquidation analysis cross-walk
   - Disclosure statement liquidation analysis must still clear best-interests (§ 1129(a)(7)) under either plan.
   - Committee’s higher going-concern EV does not automatically raise liquidation recoveries; ensure DS excerpts are updated so committee economic asks remain consistent with best-interests and feasibility.

Working-group action: paste final EV range, net debt, GUC pool, and class recovery percentages from the valuation summary schedules into Annex A before client circulation.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
V. TRANSMITTAL EMAIL — STATED COMMITTEE OBJECTIVES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The committee’s transmittal email (as referenced in the engagement materials) typically frames the redline around the following objectives. Treat these as the committee’s negotiation narrative when responding:

1. Correct alleged undervaluation in the Debtor Plan and align recoveries with a higher midpoint EV.
2. Improve GUC recoveries to a level the committee can support for solicitation.
3. Narrow non-consensual third-party releases and preserve estate causes of action (including against directors, officers, sponsors, and preference/fraudulent-transfer targets) for a GUC trust or litigation trust.
4. Obtain meaningful governance rights at Reorganized Debtor if GUCs take a material equity slice.
5. Insert committee consent / consultation rights on exit financing, rights offering backstop, and material effective-date documents.
6. Condition committee support (and any plan support agreement joinder) on incorporation of the economic package and release package in the Redline.

Deviation-report implication: economic and release articles are the “must-have” basket; technical clean-up is secondary and can be accepted more readily.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VI. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE DEVIATION ANALYSIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
Category: Technical-Drafting / Structural
Deviations (typical committee markup pattern reflected in counterparty redline practice):
- New or revised definitions: “GUC Trust,” “GUC Trust Assets,” “Litigation Claims,” “Committee Designees,” “Equity Allocation Mechanism,” “Overbid / Toggle Sale,” “Acceptable Exit Facility,” “Minimum GUC Recovery.”
- Tightening of “Related Party,” “Released Party,” and “Exculpated Party” definitions to exclude sponsors, non-debtor affiliates, and prepetition lenders except to the extent of negotiated consideration.
- Expansion of “Retained Causes of Action” schedule cross-reference.

Impact: Controls the operative scope of releases and trust funding later in the plan.
Disposition: Counter on Released Party / Exculpated Party scope; Accept useful GUC Trust definitional scaffolding if economic package agreed; confirm consistency with DS defined-terms table.

ARTICLE 2 — ADMINISTRATIVE AND PRIORITY CLAIMS
Category: Economic / Process
Deviations:
- Increased professional-fee and U.S. Trustee reserve mechanics; possible committee professional-fee carve-out clarity.
- Stricter timelines and documentation for administrative claim assertion and allowance.
- Possible elevation or separate treatment of stub rent / 503(b)(9) claims with earlier cash payment.

Impact: Cash at effective date; feasibility and exit-facility sizing.
Disposition: Accept reasonable reserve transparency; Counter if cash drain threatens exit or DIP payoff; align with valuation-summary cash build.

ARTICLE 3 — CLASSIFICATION OF CLAIMS AND INTERESTS
Category: Structural
Deviations:
- Reclassification or split of general unsecured claims (e.g., trade vs. deficiency vs. litigation; convenience class threshold raised or lowered).
- Challenge to separate classification of similarly situated unsecured claims if used to manufacture an impaired accepting class.
- Modification of equity interest classes (old common, preferred, intercompany).

Impact: § 1122 classification risk; cramdown pathway; solicitation classes.
Disposition: Reject artificial impairment or gerrymandering fixes that increase confirmation risk without economic necessity; Accept convenience-class adjustments that reduce administrative burden if recovery economics unchanged; Escalate any re-cut that alters which class is the intended impaired accepting class.

ARTICLE 4 — TREATMENT OF CLAIMS AND INTERESTS
Category: Economic (core)
Deviations:
- Secured claims: largely parallel; watch for committee push on lien challenges, adequate-protection true-ups, or replacement-lien scope.
- GUC treatment: higher recovery; form of consideration shifted (more cash and/or more reorganized equity; beneficial interests in GUC/litigation trust).
- Convenience class: modified threshold and cash-out percentage.
- Intercompany claims: remain extinguished or reinstated consistently with tax and corporate steps; committee may demand express subordination acknowledgment.
- Existing equity: cancellation with reduced or eliminated residual package; any sponsor promote or management incentive pool sized down or subjected to GUC consent.

Valuation link: Incremental EV at committee midpoint is the stated source of improved GUC recoveries.
DS link: Treatment tables and recovery illustrations in disclosure statement excerpts must be conformed; risk factors on equity wipeout and trust recoveries need update.
Disposition: Counter with a bracketed GUC recovery range tied to a joint valuation protocol or updated third-party valuation; Reject open-ended true-up that makes effective-date economics indeterminate; Escalate residual equity / MIP sizing to client and sponsor (if any).

ARTICLE 5 — MEANS OF IMPLEMENTATION
Category: Structural / Economic / Governance
Deviations:
- GUC Trust or Litigation Trust formation, funding amount, governance (committee-selected trustee), and claim-objection coordination.
- Rights offering / equity allocation mechanism: GUC participation percentage; backstop fee sharing; oversubscription.
- Exit facility: definition of Acceptable Exit Facility; committee consultation or consent right on material terms.
- Corporate steps: merger, conversion, new holding company; issuance of New Common Stock percentages by constituency.
- Toggle / marketing process: committee may insert a toggle to a § 363 or plan sale if exit financing or equity raise fails, with committee consultation.

Impact: Feasibility, absolute priority, and post-effective-date value leakage.
Disposition: Accept GUC trust architecture if funded from agreed envelope; Counter on backstop fees and equity split; Reject unilateral committee veto over ordinary-course exit terms; Accept information rights and consultation on material financing docs.

ARTICLE 6 — GOVERNANCE OF REORGANIZED DEBTOR
Category: Governance
Deviations:
- Board size and composition: committee designees (e.g., 1–2 seats) if GUCs take material equity.
- Observer rights, information rights, and minority protective provisions (related-party transactions, incremental debt, affiliate deals).
- Management incentive plan (MIP) pool percentage reduced or subject to new board approval with independent director consent.
- Officer employment / KERP-KEIP carryover scrutiny.

Impact: Control of Reorganized Debtor; marketability of new equity; management retention.
Disposition: Escalate board seats and protective provisions to client; Counter MIP to market (typical 5–10% range depending on case) with independent-director process; Accept information rights proportionate to GUC equity stake.

ARTICLE 7 — DISTRIBUTIONS
Category: Technical / Economic
Deviations:
- Distribution record dates, disputed claims reserves, and true-up mechanics favoring earlier interim GUC distributions.
- Unclaimed property to GUC trust rather than reorganized debtor.
- Withholding and tax reporting aligned with trust structure.

Disposition: Accept if operationally workable with claims agent; Counter if interim distributions impair working capital or exit covenants.

ARTICLE 8 — EXECUTORY CONTRACTS AND UNEXPIRED LEASES
Category: Economic / Process
Deviations:
- Broader assumption/rejection schedule transparency; committee consultation on material contract assumption costs.
- Cure objection procedures tightened; possible reservation of rights on landlord claims and 502(b)(6) caps.
- Employee agreements and benefit plans: committee may demand review of insider agreements assumed under the plan.

Disposition: Accept process transparency; Counter on any blanket committee consent right over ordinary-course assumptions; Escalate insider contract assumptions.

ARTICLE 9 — RELEASES, EXCULPATION, INJUNCTIONS, AND RELATED PROVISIONS
Category: Release-Injunction (high sensitivity)
Deviations:
- Debtor releases: generally retained but with expanded retained-causes-of-action schedule carved out for GUC/litigation trust.
- Third-party releases: narrowed; non-consensual third-party releases limited or eliminated as to sponsors, D&Os (except for specified covered conduct), and non-debtor affiliates, unless opt-in or substantial contribution shown.
- Exculpation: limited to estate fiduciaries and estate professionals for postpetition conduct; remove or cabin prepetition actors.
- Injunction: conforms to narrowed release scope; gateways for trust litigation preserved.
- Gatekeeping / claim-objection bar dates coordinated so released claims are not inadvertently preserved or extinguished inconsistently with trust deed.

Legal / market context: Post-Purdue and evolving circuit law on non-consensual third-party releases; disclosure and consent mechanics are critical. DS excerpts must clearly describe release scope, opt-out/opt-in, and consideration.
Disposition: Accept narrowing that reduces confirmation risk and preserves legitimate estate claims for creditors; Reject any committee attempt to use release leverage without settling the economic package; Counter with opt-out structure, clear consideration recital, and tailored D&O coverage if insured and value-accretive; Escalate final release matrix to partner and client.

ARTICLE 10 — CONDITIONS PRECEDENT; EFFECTIVE DATE; TOGGLE
Category: Process-Condition
Deviations:
- Additional conditions: entry of acceptable confirmation order (with release language as redlined); funding of GUC trust; execution of trust agreement and new governance documents in form acceptable to committee; exit facility in Acceptable Exit Facility form.
- Committee termination rights if economics drift below Minimum GUC Recovery.
- Toggle to sale process if conditions fail by outside date.

Disposition: Accept ordinary documentation conditions; Counter on open-ended “form acceptable to committee” standards — replace with “reasonably acceptable” and agreed term sheets; Reject conditions that give committee a free option to unwind after other constituencies are locked.

ARTICLE 11 — MODIFICATION, REVOCATION, WITHDRAWAL
Category: Process
Deviations:
- Limits on debtor’s unilateral modification post-solicitation without committee consent if modification adversely affects GUC treatment.
Disposition: Accept adverse-effect consent right consistent with plan support agreement norms; Counter on consent rights over immaterial or technical modifications.

ARTICLE 12 — RETENTION OF JURISDICTION; MISCELLANEOUS
Category: Technical
Deviations:
- Explicit retention for GUC trust disputes, claim objections, and release-enforcement matters.
Disposition: Accept.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VII. DISCLOSURE STATEMENT EXCERPTS — CONFORMING CHANGES REQUIRED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The disclosure statement excerpts must be updated in lockstep with any accepted redlines. Priority DS conformity items:

1. Plan summary and treatment tables — GUC and equity rows.
2. Valuation and recovery illustrations — replace debtor midpoint with agreed midpoint or dual-case presentation; explain methodology differences flagged in valuation summary.
3. Liquidation analysis — confirm best-interests still satisfied; revise narrative if GUC trust changes residual value story.
4. Releases / exculpation / injunctions section — plain-English description, opt-out/opt-in mechanics, parties released, claims released, and consideration.
5. Risk factors — litigation-trust recovery uncertainty; governance change; equity cancellation; exit-financing conditionality; toggle-sale risk.
6. Solicitation and voting — class composition changes; convenience class; ballots for opt-out.
7. Feasibility — cash uses at effective date including trust seed funding and admin reserves.
8. Certain U.S. federal income tax consequences — trust classification (grantor vs. complex), new equity, cancellation of indebtedness.
9. Alternatives to confirmation — including committee’s asserted superior recoveries under alternative structures.

Until DS excerpts are conformed, do not commence solicitation on a hybrid plan.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VIII. CONFIRMATION-RISK MATRIX
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Issue                              | Debtor Plan risk      | Committee Redline effect           | Net
----------------------------------|-----------------------|------------------------------------|------------------
§ 1129(a)(7) best interests       | Manageable if LA ok   | Usually still ok if cash/trust ↑   | Neutral / better
§ 1129(a)(11) feasibility         | Depends on exit       | Higher cash out / trust seed       | Watch cash
Absolute priority / residual eq.  | Equity thin residual  | Harder equity wipe may help APR    | Better if clean
Unfair discrimination             | Class split risk      | Reclass may help or hurt           | Case-specific
Good faith § 1129(a)(3)           | Standard              | Support letter helps if economics  | Better if deal
Third-party releases              | Overbreadth risk      | Narrowing reduces appeal risk      | Better
Impaired accepting class          | Depends on structure  | GUC impairment clearer             | Often better
Indubitable equivalent / secured  | Standard              | Minimal change if liens respected  | Neutral

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
IX. CONSOLIDATED DEVIATION LOG (NEGOTIATION CHART)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

No. | Topic                         | Debtor Plan position           | Committee Redline                         | Category   | Recommended disposition
----|-------------------------------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|------------|-------------------------
1   | Enterprise value midpoint     | Debtor valuation               | Higher midpoint per valuation summary     | Economic   | Counter — joint valuation protocol / bracket
2   | GUC recovery % / form         | Lower; cash+thin equity        | Higher; cash+equity+trust interests       | Economic   | Counter — tie to agreed EV and claims pool
3   | GUC / Litigation Trust        | Limited or none                | Funded trust; committee trustee           | Structural | Accept in principle; negotiate seed $ and claim scope
4   | Existing equity residual      | Warrants / thin residual       | Cancel / de minimis                       | Economic   | Escalate — client/sponsor
5   | MIP / management equity       | Debtor-proposed pool           | Reduced pool; board process               | Governance | Counter to market; independent director approval
6   | Board composition             | Debtor/sponsor slate           | Committee designee seat(s)                | Governance | Escalate — proportionate to GUC equity %
7   | Exit facility consent         | Debtor control                 | Committee consent / Acceptable Facility   | Process    | Counter — consultation + “reasonably acceptable”
8   | Rights offering / backstop    | Debtor/sponsor backstop        | GUC participation / fee share             | Economic   | Counter — allocation grid in term sheet
9   | Third-party releases          | Broad non-debtor releases      | Narrowed; opt-in/opt-out; carve-outs      | Releases   | Accept narrowing; settle consideration narrative
10  | Exculpation scope             | Broad                          | Estate fiduciaries / postpetition only    | Releases   | Accept market formulation
11  | Retained causes of action     | Limited schedule               | Expanded schedule to trust                | Structural | Accept with defined non-released core claims
12  | Classification / convenience  | Debtor classes                 | Re-bucket GUCs; adjust convenience        | Structural | Accept if no gerrymander; else Reject
13  | Admin / professional reserves | Debtor estimates               | Higher transparency / cushion             | Economic   | Accept reasonable; protect exit cash
14  | Effective-date conditions     | Standard                       | Trust funding; docs OK to committee; min recovery | Process | Counter open-ended approval standards
15  | Toggle / sale fallback        | Limited                        | Toggle if financing fails                 | Process    | Accept with shared milestones; no free option
16  | Plan modification rights      | Debtor flexibility             | GUC adverse-effect consent                | Process    | Accept PSA-style adverse-effect consent
17  | DS recovery illustrations     | Debtor figures                 | Must conform to redline economics         | Disclosure | Required conformity before solicitation
18  | Definitions (Released Party)  | Broad                          | Narrow                                    | Technical  | Align to final release matrix

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
X. OPEN ISSUES FOR PARTNER / CLIENT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Agree valuation midpoint (or dual-track disclosure) with reference to the valuation summary schedules; decide whether to commission a refreshed independent valuation.
2. Set maximum GUC economic package (cash + equity % + trust seed) that remains feasible under exit-facility and working-capital constraints.
3. Decide residual equity / warrant package, if any, for old equity and sponsor.
4. Board: number of committee designees vs. independent directors vs. sponsor/debtor carryover.
5. Final release matrix and opt-out mechanics given applicable circuit law and U.S. Trustee positions.
6. Whether to seek a plan support agreement with the committee incorporating the settled economic and release package.
7. Solicitation timeline impact of DS revisions and any resolicitation risk if modifications are material post-solicitation.
8. Tax structure of GUC trust and new equity issuance (coordinate with tax counsel).
9. Claims-pool estimation disputes that could erase the apparent recovery uplift even at committee EV.
10. Confirm all bracketed figures in Annex A against the full valuation summary, complete redline, and full disclosure statement (not only excerpts).

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
XI. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Populate Annex A with final numbers from the valuation summary and claims-agent reports.
2. Prepare a reverse redline / issues list responding to the committee markup using the disposition column in Section IX.
3. Schedule a working-group call (debtor, sponsor if any, committee) focused on EV midpoint, GUC envelope, and release matrix only — defer technical drafting until economic handshake.
4. Instruct DS counsel to draft conforming disclosure statement revisions in parallel once economics are bracketed.
5. Run confirmation-risk refresh under §§ 1129(a) and (b) after the economic handshake.
6. If settlement reached, document in a plan support agreement or plan term sheet before revising operative plan documents.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
XII. ANNEX A — VALUATION & RECOVERY WORKPAPER (TO BE COMPLETED FROM EXHIBITS)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
XIII. ANNEX B — RELEASE MATRIX WORKPAPER

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
